assumptions: Clinical decisions based on standard first-aid priorities (ILCOR/AHA/ERC style): airway/breathing/circulation threats, neurological red flags (FAST+), systemic envenomation signs, and mechanism-of-injury markers take precedence for ranking and escalation.
General symptoms (dizziness, nausea, confusion, sweating_cold) are multi-case by nature; only added to match where they meaningfully improve ranking without diluting specificity.
Specific scene markers (saw_snake, scorpion_seen, amputated_part, open_fracture, electrical_contact, etc.) left untouched.
Schema rule enforced: any new red or emergency implies risk=true.

changes.reason: Difficulty breathing is a core systemic feature of anaphylaxis and should contribute to ranking this case; currently only in riskQuestions.
Syncope/fainting is a recognised systemic sign of anaphylactic shock and improves ranking when present with other allergic markers.
Dizziness/vertigo is a common presenting feature of posterior-circulation stroke and should contribute a modest match weight; currently only risk.
Dizziness or light-headedness frequently accompanies acute coronary syndromes and aids ranking alongside chest pain and autonomic signs.
Cyanosis during choking indicates severe hypoxia and must appear in riskQuestions so the user is prompted; currently only match.
Cyanosis in the context of choking warrants immediate emergency activation in addition to the existing choking_signs trigger.
Multiple stings already trigger emergencyCall; adding to redFlags makes the escalation path consistent and surfaces the systemic risk flag.
Cyanosis is already a high-stakes red/emergency marker; raising its match weight from 3 to 4 better reflects its ranking importance for severe respiratory distress.
Aligns weight with clinical severity already encoded in redFlags and emergencyCall.
Confusion is a key differentiator for both hypo- and hyperglycaemia and deserves a slightly higher match weight than the current 2.
Improves ranking priority for altered mental status in known diabetics.
Cold/pale skin is part of the classic shock picture and complements the existing shock_signs and sweating_cold matches.
Cyanosis is a common observation in opioid-induced respiratory depression and should help rank this case.
Cyanosis should prompt the risk question list for opioid overdose.
Seizure is already an emergency trigger; giving it a modest match weight improves ranking when present with substance exposure.
Post-traumatic dizziness is a frequent and clinically relevant symptom that should contribute to ranking head-injury.
Dizziness after head impact belongs in the risk question set.
Respiratory involvement is a critical systemic sign of envenomation; currently only risk/red; modest match weight improves ranking.
Same rationale as snake-bite: respiratory distress is a key systemic marker and should influence ranking.
Inhalation injury (already flagged via soot_nose) can present with difficulty breathing; adding the symptom itself to riskQuestions covers cases without visible soot.
Difficulty breathing after a burn (especially with facial/soot involvement) is an emergency trigger.
Chest pain accompanying syncope markedly raises the possibility of cardiac cause and should influence ranking.
Occasional gasps in an unresponsive but 'breathing' patient may indicate agonal respiration; should appear in riskQuestions.

notes: No propose_new_case suggestions; the existing case set already covers the major first-aid domains.
Specific markers (amputated_part, open_fracture, saw_snake, scorpion_seen, electrical_contact, drowning_recent, tooth_knocked_out, tick_attached, etc.) deliberately left unchanged.
Weights kept conservative (mostly 2–4) to avoid over-ranking common symptoms.
All new red/emergency additions are paired with risk=true to satisfy schema.
If human review prefers stricter specificity, the dizziness and cold_skin additions can be dropped without harming core safety pathways.
warnings: Adding cyanosis to choking emergencyCall and difficulty_breathing to thermal-burn emergencyCall slightly expands the always-call surface; clinically justified but worth human confirmation against local protocol.
Match-weight increases for cyanosis (breathing-difficulty) and confusion (diabetic-emergency) are modest; if ranking behaviour is already satisfactory they can be left at current values.
